comments.body: `containsAny` is matched with `.every(...)`, which means "contains all". The server's `containsAny` runs `"col"::text[] && ARRAY[...]` (compute-where-condition-parts.ts, added in this diff), which is an overlap, so any one match is enough. Take a filter with `containsAny: ['A','B']` and a record whose value is `['A']`. The server returns the record. `isRecordMatchingFilter` (isRecordMatchingFilter.ts, the MultiSelect case) says it doesn't match. Optimistic create and update (`triggerCreateRecordsOptimisticEffect.ts:90`, `triggerUpdateRecordOptimisticEffect.ts:68`) then drop or never add records that belong in the filtered list. The `DoesNotContain` branch wraps this in `not`, so it gets the opposite error. It needs `some`.

`computeViewRecordGqlOperationFilter` builds the ARRAY filter as ``containsIlike: `%${filter.value}%` `` (the new `case 'ARRAY'`). Here the client lowercases that string and calls `item.toLowerCase().includes(searchTerm)`. `includes` treats the `%` characters literally, so `searchTerm` is `"%foo%"` and no item ever matches. For an Array field with a Contains filter on "foo", the server returns matching rows. The client-side matcher returns false for every record, so optimistic cache updates wrongly exclude them. `DoesNotContain` is wrong the other way. The matcher should strip the `%` wildcards, or implement ILIKE semantics.
